newsitem.title: USA: Plans set for changes in nuclear weapon complex.
newsitem.headline: Plans set for changes in nuclear weapon complex.

text.p: The Energy Department Thursday signed off on final plans to start construction and operation of three new facilities to maintain the nation's nuclear weapons without underground testing or producing new weapons.

A document signed by Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary also will allow the department to start shrinking weapons-related operations at the Oak Ridge Plant in Tennessee, the Pantex Plant in Texas and the Kansas City Plant in Missouri.

"With the end of the Cold War, the Department of Energy's weapons laboratories and production plants are now focused on warhead dismantlement and assuring the safety and reliability of the remaining stockpile without underground nuclear tests," O'Leary said in a statement.

As part of a $4 billion-a-year program, the department will build additional testing facilities at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in California and at Los Alamos National Laboratory in New Mexico.

Also at Los Alamos, the department said it will establish "a small capability to make plutonium pits" or nuclear weapons cores, which have not been fabricated since the closing of the Rocky Flats Plant in Colorado in 1992.

The department said it will start reducing operations at the three plants in 1998. That process is expected to cost about $170 million, which the department said should be recouped by 2003 and result in a total savings of about $1 billion by 2010.

A coalition of environmental and anti-nuclear groups called the Military Production Network said it intended to sue to block the department from carrying out the plan that it said would be create "dangerous, irrelevant programs."
